title: Participation counts: Prevention of occupational cancer with a focus on people with a history of migration
summary:
More than a quarter of the population in Germany has a migration background. This group is very heterogeneous in terms of various characteristics (e.g. age, income, social status, occupational and educational qualifications) and also differs to some extent from people without a migration background. For example, there is evidence of health-related differences between people with and without a migration background. A comparatively high number of accidents at work and occupational illnesses are suspected among people with a migrant background, which may be associated with long periods of absence from work. In addition, people with a migrant background are sometimes less likely to undergo early detection tests (e.g. cancer screening) or to make use of other health promotion or occupational safety and health services. 

Designing and implementing good working conditions plays a key role in preventing work-related illnesses. Different sectors and activities pose different work-related risks. For example, workers in construction and agriculture need special protection against occupational cancers of the lung or skin. These sectors also employ a high proportion of migrant workers from a variety of backgrounds and activities, such as skilled workers living in Germany or seasonal workers from abroad. In addition to technical and work organization measures taken by employers (e.g., installing asbestos locks, installing shade structures, scheduling lunch breaks, offering counseling and screening), the implementation of work-related cancer prevention and early detection measures in many areas of activity in these sectors relies heavily on the cooperation of employees. These include, for example, taking breaks in the shade, applying sunscreen, and wearing weather-appropriate clothing and respirators. In addition to a targeted approach, it is essential to increase the understanding and acceptance of protective measures.  

To our knowledge, there has not been a systematic survey of the needs, barriers and facilitators for the prevention and early detection of occupational cancer with a focus on people with a migration background. This survey is an essential basis for the development of practice-oriented measures that are accepted and implemented by those affected. Against this background, we are researching the needs, barriers and intervention potentials for the prevention and early detection of occupational cancer among people with and without a migration background, using the example of the construction and agricultural sectors, together with interest holders from the field - e.g. people working in the construction and agricultural sectors, experts in the field of health prevention.

In order to do justice to the diversity of the fields of activity and the people employed in these two sectors, we collect the data in a variety of ways that are as low-threshold as possible. The main data build participant observations and ethnographic or informal interviews with people working in different workplaces (2x agriculture, 2x construction). The first step will be to identify barriers and facilitators from the perspective of relevant stakeholders in order to derive core themes. Based on preliminary results, potentials to improve access, use and implementation of prevention and early detection of occupational cancer will be developed in cooperation between science and practice. In addition, the possibility of transferring the results to other sectors and other cancers or carcinogenic effects will be explored. We expect that the results of our study will provide a sound, practice-oriented basis for the development of target-group-specific interventions, particularly in the areas of occupational safety culture and work-related health literacy, for the prevention of occupational cancer in other sectors and for other exposures.
conditions: Prevention of occupational cancers related to asbestos and UV radiation

interventions.name:
Participant observations (n = 4) at two construction sites and two farms and interviews with key informants (n~20).

Workshops (n=5)  with key informants, other experts in workplace practice, prevention and early detection.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Inclusion criteria are working in the field at participating companies and consent to participate in the study.
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion criteria are refusal to participate in the study. Patients and minors are excluded from the study.
